svg.title: Baseline management group hierarchy of the Azure landing zone
svg.desc: Layout follows the management group hierarchy in the official documentation. Three bands of management groups, each with its own band of subscriptions below it: Platform, Landing zones, and Decommissioned with Sandboxes. Tenant root group is the top, then the intermediate root management group. Under it: Platform with the child groups Security, Management, Identity and Connectivity, each with a dedicated subscription; Landing zones with Corp, Online and Local, plus a dashed example group PCI that is added only if a requirement needs it; Corp has workload landing zone subscriptions A1, P1 and A2; Local has two workload landing zone subscriptions, one for Azure Local clusters and one for applications; Decommissioned with a decommissioned subscription, deleted by Azure after 30 to 60 days; Sandboxes with two sandbox subscriptions. Notes say that if you need to separate development, test and production, you use separate subscriptions in the same management group, and that the hierarchy should ideally be three or four levels. Icons are official Azure icons.
svg.text: Example only, if a need arises
If you need to separate development, test and production, use separate subscriptions
in the same management group, not separate management groups.
Ideally keep it to three or four levels (Azure allows up to six, not counting the tenant root group or subscriptions).
Add new archetype groups only under Landing zones or Platform.
